precepts.text: Every day they wrest my words; they gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul. TikTok's new terms track your location and even immigration status.
precepts.point: His eyes are privily set against the poor: the eye on the dollar, the surveillance that sees every site you visit and, through the ADL and the police systems, every bank account. He lieth in wait secretly as a lion to catch the poor when he draweth him into his net, and the poor fall by his strong ones, the police and the military.

note.label: Cyber Warfare: The Mouth Of The Beast

precepts.why:
The wicked sits in the secret places and “his eyes are privily set against the poor.” David describes how they watch: “Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil. They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul.”

They mark your steps: they watch everywhere you go. When you download TikTok now, you have to agree to terms that let them check your immigration status and follow your location wherever you go. The new terms are set up to monitor you and follow you. They want to destroy our soul.

Christ went through the same thing: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.” They watch us through these devices; even YouTube lets our channels stay up so they can monitor us. And they send spies who act righteous and act like they want to learn, sent by the federal government to set us up, plant something and lie on us, as they did in France, where conversations among the brothers showed up in the court case against a brother put out of the country.

That is why anything you say has to be scriptural; none of you should be saying dumb, stupid stuff, because they are waiting to wrest your words and deliver them to the government. And the one who takes that work for a little house and a little bank account condemns his soul forever. But the Lord “disappointeth the devices of the crafty”, and “he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth”: from the lies of their media.

precepts.text: Fear not them that kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather fear Him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
precepts.point: In God he praises His word and puts his trust, and will not fear what flesh can do. This does not mean you never experience fear, but you will not put the fear of man over the fear of God or let it stand between you and the mission.

note.label: Psalm 56: I Will Not Fear What Flesh Can Do Unto Me

precepts.why:
“What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee. In God I will praise his word, in God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.” Christ says the same: “fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.”

This does not mean you never experience fear. Man would swallow David up, fighting daily and oppressing him, and he says what time I am afraid. But you will not put the fear of man over the fear of God, or let it stand between you and the mission. Flesh can kill the body and no more; the one to fear is the one who can destroy both soul and body in hell.

precepts.text: The scribes and Pharisees provoked Christ, laying wait to catch something out of His mouth to accuse Him, wicked enough to provoke the Son of the living God.
precepts.point: He asks whether they shall escape by iniquity, and trusts that the Most High tells his wanderings and keeps his tears in a bottle, and that his enemies shall turn back because God is for him.

note.label: Psalm 56: I Will Not Fear What Flesh Can Do Unto Me

precepts.why:
“Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil. They gather themselves together, they hide themselves, they mark my steps, when they wait for my soul.” This is David in the spirit foreseeing what would happen to Christ. “the scribes and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, and to provoke him to speak of many things: Laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him.”

They provoked Christ and lay in wait to catch something out of his mouth to accuse him; they wrested his words every day and marked his steps. They were wicked enough to provoke the Son of the living God. And as David said, shall they escape by iniquity? God is for him, and his enemies turn back.

points: He asks for mercy because man would swallow him up, fighting daily and oppressing him, for many fight against him. What time he is afraid, he will trust in the Most High.
